title: Breakfast, Fossils, and New Recruits
synopsis: Movie 10 opens with the usual ground rules and a roster of new toy recruits joining the family, including Bruisey and Whitestripe, a baby Bionicle and Tohunga, twin babies Jewelize and Emeril, and a batch of Transformers. The story then drops into a chaotic toy-family breakfast and schoolroom skit, complete with a math lesson and a running gag about a 'fossilized' pet lizard. It closes by setting up the real plot: the Toa and Turaga must scour the islands for platinum masks and mysterious silver crowns ahead of the coming Universal War.

title: Fossils, Bloopers, and Battle Plans
synopsis: More of the toy-family morning skit plays out, with the kids' 'dead pet lizard' turned into a cracked-skull show-and-tell and a late-night blooper moment before bed. The narrator then breaks in to explain the real mission: the Toa and Turaga must track down the Bohrok Kal and search for platinum masks and silver crowns, and battle plans start getting sketched out in the kitchen.

title: Charting the Search for the Bohrok Kal
synopsis: After a classroom detour, complete with a 'daily individual reading time' bit and a nail-painting break, the narrator lays toy figures out as map markers for the Toa and Turaga and dispatches them toward Ga-Koro and the other villages. A Toa suits up with a Krana and Kanohi mask and heads off in search of the Bohrok Kal, kicking off the real quest.

title: Awakening Tarnok Ka
synopsis: The narrator purifies a Krana to awaken and recruit a new Bohrok Kal ally, talked out of loyalty to the Barraki and into joining the Super Family. Night-vision Kanohi powers and a bit of hide-and-seek lead into the hunt for another Bohrok Kal, before the episode wraps with a costume-change musical number from the toy background singers.

title: The Waterfall Krana
synopsis: The hunt for another Bohrok Kal turns up a Krana tumbling down a waterfall instead, which the crew purifies and uses to awaken and recruit a new ally who agrees to defect from the Barraki. The search then moves into the jungle, where the group closes in on yet another Bohrok Kal to awaken.

title: Power Shields and New Allies
synopsis: A scrappy toy battle plays out over borrowed 'power shields' and locked-up weak spots, ending with another Bohrok Kal talked into abandoning the Barraki for the Super Family. A further new recruit is introduced before the narrator cues up the next big musical and dance number with the full cast of background singers.

title: Pop Live in Mexico
synopsis: A brief, mostly musical interlude built around a dance number introduced as 'Pop live in Mexico,' interrupted by a quick skirmish featuring one of the heroes showing off a plasma power and a shiny mask. It closes with another Bohrok Kal agreeing to join the Super Family.

title: The Last of the Bohrok Kal
synopsis: A goofy, gross-out battle full of jokes about who 'tastes like chicken wings' wraps up the Bohrok Kal hunt as the last holdouts are defeated and their masks swapped from gold to platinum. The narrator, in character as Tahu the Toa, gives a closing address thanking the audience and teasing the next movie: the coming Universal War and the mystery of the seventh Toa.

title: Attack on Gamblia
synopsis: Movie 11 opens with the usual rules and a roster of new toy recruits, then jumps straight into crisis: news breaks of an attack on Gamblia, and the family's evil sister plots to sabotage the AC's shield generator with her mask of darkness. Dr. Senor rallies the massed troops for all-out war, delivering a chilling 'show no mercy' order as the Universal War begins.

title: Storm Before the War
synopsis: A short, quiet stretch in which the narrator and a companion watch the sky suddenly darken and storm as the troops are called up, reading it as an ominous sign of the war to come. Little happens beyond wary small talk about the weather turning grim.

title: A Silent Skirmish
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action, with no narrated dialogue to describe what unfolds.

title: Into the Fray
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action as the Universal War continues, with little to no narrated dialogue.

title: The Battle Rages On
synopsis: Another dialogue-free stretch of toy-battle action, with the war playing out entirely in silent stop-motion.

title: No Words, Just War
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion combat with no narration to guide it, presumably more Universal War fighting.

title: Deep in the Universal War
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action, with little to no narrated dialogue over this segment.

title: The Fighting Continues
synopsis: A dialogue-light stretch of ongoing stop-motion battle action, with essentially no narration captured on this segment.

title: Cereal, New Recruits, and a Vow
synopsis: Movie 12 opens with a wave of new recruits, including baby badgers Moonglaze and Sun Giant, new Transformers, and more babies, introduced from the family's underground hideout while Makuta lurks nearby. A parody cereal-box breakfast bit, complete with 'Kopaka Sugar-Frosted Sugar-Coated Sugar Lumps' and 'Lavok's Super-Sour Acid Blasts,' leads into a tense debate over whether to strike Makuta that very night.

title: Halftime: Toy Football
synopsis: A breather episode away from the war plot: the toy cast splits into color-coded teams, complete with captains and goalies, for a game of football before the main story resumes.

title: Sneaking Past the Battle Droids
synopsis: The team is called to the launching pad to make their move after word arrives that their location may have been found. They sabotage a security camera and turn captured battle droids against their own side as they slip toward the exit.

title: Enter the Rahkshi
synopsis: The heroes finally track Makuta down for their rematch, only for him to unveil his newest secret weapon: the Rahkshi, which he boasts are the most powerful beings in the universe.

title: Lightsabers Against Makuta
synopsis: A wild toy brawl against Makuta and his Rahkshi devolves into pure parody, complete with a mock lightsaber duel, a 'hyper beam,' and jabs about broken parts and stolen masks. A running gag about Makuta having a secret wife and son caps the chaos, with the family's new baby badgers making their debut in the fight.

title: Makuta's True Form
synopsis: Makuta debates unveiling his 'true form' as three towering new monster allies join the fray to back him up. The battle turns silly with a hover-car bit and a running gag about corn flour, before the narrator teases the family's newest batch of baby recruits.

title: Whose Kids Win the War
synopsis: Amid the ongoing fight, the narrator and Makuta trade boasts about whose toy family has more babies, introducing a new arrival with a whip-like tail. A mock 'doctor's visit' bit and a musical cue close out the segment.

title: Second Grade Bragging Rights
synopsis: A very brief comic beat where the narrator taunts Makuta that being in second grade now gives the Super Family the edge over him, a quick joke-driven breather in the ongoing war.

title: Roxy Joins the Battle
synopsis: The Rahkshi wade deeper into a chaotic fight full of gross-out gags, including 'oatmeal' that shatters stomachs and a mega-laser attack, plus a running joke about cereal cows liking too much. The segment ends with the debut of Roxy, unleashed with a cupcake attack and a confusion power against Makuta's side.

title: Grandma Spoils the Kids
synopsis: A real-life baby crying and spelling jokes about "poopy" bleed into the toy battle as the narrator debates a force field versus a force shield. Pikachu and Aku Aku show up for a surprise cameo, and someone teases the enemy about "forgetting" their weak spots on purpose. A quick invincibility attack wraps up a scattered, giggly stretch of play.

title: The Mini-Cons Join the Battle
synopsis: New allies roll in as a Transformer introduces his tiny partner, a Mini-Con named Joel, and the powerful Star Saber, joining the fight against Makuta. Between "chew chew chew" sound effects and a Hyper Hydraulic Cannon transformation, the newcomer boasts that he's finally strong enough to take down the Super Family's foe. A boom box tags along for good measure.

title: The Evil Shot Doctor Makes House Calls
synopsis: The narrator fumbles with a boom box and a Transformers catalog before diving into a pile-on against the Rock Sheep. A self-declared "Evil Shot Doctor" threatens to give the Rock Sheep a very unwelcome checkup, while a shield built for a "Hyper Supernova Beam" gets tried on for size. Mini-Con Shab causes more trouble than help along the way.

title: Optimus Prime and Jetfire Arrive
synopsis: The Transformers lineup grows as Optimus Prime and Jetfire roll in, combining forces with their Mini-Cons to battle Makuta. Between jabs about broken toys getting thrown out the window and a scolding over "stealing heads," this segment is short on plot but big on new arrivals. It ends just as Jetfire and his partner prepare to fight.

title: Jab, Jab, Jab: The Krona Mix-Up
synopsis: Jetfire trades blows while the narrator's characters bicker over what to even call their brain-stone canisters, fumbling between "Krata," "karma," and "Krona." Between sword fights and a joke about keeping stingers safe in tiny capes, the fighters admit their attacks are getting a little too intense for a "rated G" show. A running gag about mixed-up names carries most of the episode.

title: The Bohrok-Kal's Wrong Krona
synopsis: A parade of specialty Krona -- radar-sense, tunneling, telepathy, and flying -- gets swapped in and out as the heroes battle a lineup of Bohrok, including one called Lirok. Rubber bands double as makeshift gear to hold the brain-stones in place, and a "translation" Krona lets one fighter claim he can talk to the ground. It's a scrappy, joke-heavy stretch built on toy-mechanic experimentation more than plot.

title: The Infected Mask Sticky Thing
synopsis: A tongue-twisting new weapon -- the "infected mask sticky thingy" -- gets debuted alongside a chainsaw hand-attachment and a knock-knock joke to match. The heroes trade quips about drinking, driving, and homonyms between rounds while still needling Makuta. A Krona that lets its wearer "talk to the landscape" adds one more oddball power to the pile.

title: The Mask That Tastes Like Chocolate
synopsis: A fighter shows off a big-cheeked mask that sharpens every sense at once -- sight, smell, taste, even the claimed ability to "hear ice cream." A color-coordination squabble over red versus yellow breaks out mid-battle, and someone insists they can taste chocolate that isn't really there. It's a lighter, gag-heavy stretch built around sensory-power jokes.

title: The Leaders of Bohrok Strike Back
synopsis: Self-proclaimed "leaders of Bohrok" square off against the heroes, flinging Krona and bragging they won't be beaten as easily as last time. Between near-misses and a running joke about how dangerous it is to "play with weapons," the fighters cycle through flying, radar, and sensing Krona. A giant marine-type Bohrok gets revived just as the segment wraps up.

title: Who's Your Daddy, Makuta?
synopsis: A long, chaotic brawl runs through mask swaps, kneeling contests, and a riff on "who's your daddy" before settling into a war of attrition over Kaita energy. Fighters trade freeze, acid, and "freezer burn" attacks while bickering about who's older, taller, and dumber. By the end, one side is visibly falling apart from the energy loss.

title: Tigger Crashes the Battle
synopsis: A hundred-acre-wood detour brings Piglet and an unstoppable, bouncing Tigger into the middle of a Rahkshi fight, and "Tiggers cannot be defeated by evil Rahkshi" becomes the episode's rallying cry. One hero's love shield proves immune to both poison and energy-draining, while a healing cocoa attack and a hypnosis move round out the arsenal. It's a giddy, bounce-heavy stretch of toy-battle chaos.

title: Agent 9, Sheila, and the Color Drain
synopsis: New fighters Agent 9 and Sheila join a battle full of monkey beams and mask-collecting, as the heroes explain they're gathering "infected" masks to turn evil ones nice again. A rival's signature attack drains all the color out of its target, leaving them "blurry" and cartoonishly old. Sibling banter about "worst nightmares" threads through the fight.

title: Turok's Heart Attack Trick
synopsis: A short, chant-heavy stretch opens with a "chika raka chika boom" cheer before rolling into a battle featuring Turok, the Drainer, and the Shatterer. The plan: make the enemies "so angry at each other" that they turn on themselves, no attack required. A mega laser gets teased but never quite lands.

title: Doctor Pon Rock's Exploding Shots
synopsis: A dust-powered fighter trades quips about Swiffers before the newly "graduated" medical specialist Pon Rock steals the show, threatening enemies with shots that make things explode. Between jokes about who's really Makuta's kid, a rival group is introduced almost as an afterthought. Everyone suits back up just as the segment ends.

title: Meet Mr. Fist
synopsis: A shape-shifting box-vehicle joins the fray, and the heroes tease the debut of a new form nicknamed "Mr. Fist." Jokes about staffs looking like pine cones and a Chrono shield that blocks other Chrono attacks pepper a battle built on escalating power boasts. One fighter claims he tricked an enemy into handing over all his power -- then finished him off.

title: The Mask of Concealment
synopsis: A hero shows off the noble Kanohi mask of concealment, going invisible mid-fight while everyone argues over whether a particular mask is really "infected." A newly arrived Toa in platinum armor joins in with rapid slashing attacks, teasing there's more power still to come. Nuparu gets a hit in of his own before the segment wraps.

title: The Great Kicking Contest
synopsis: Toa Platinum fighter Pohatu and a partner unleash an absurdly long barrage of kicks -- so long the narrator loses count -- while gloating about their shiny new platinum masks. Between water-versus-fire banter and a bit about "barbecuing" a mask, Turok gets branded "the master of fear" and a fallen ally turns out to be back from the dead. It's a loud, repetitive brawl heavy on sound effects.

title: The Masks of Mind Control and Time
synopsis: A Kanohi mask of mind control and a mask of time make their debut in a heated exchange packed with masks flying off left and right. Nui Jaga insects join the fray, and one fighter powers up with an X-ray-vision mask while explaining he "can't punch very fast" until he rebuilds his legs. Plenty of mask-knockoffs, not much explanation.

title: The Turaga Nui's Seven Masks
synopsis: A legendary being called the Turaga Nui takes the stage, boasting a special mask that never comes off and daring the heroes to knock away all seven of his masks to win. Between freeze beams and a fear-draining attack, he needles Makuta for talking "like an old guy" while guarding his mask of time to the very end. A tense standoff closes out the segment.

title: The Care Bears Sing-Along
synopsis: Between sword-in-the-head jokes and a Tigger callback, the battle grinds to a halt for a full musical number about clubbing Care Bears, followed by an unrelated song roasting a "fat guy." Toa Nuva fighters square off against a Rahkshi built from scavenged pieces once the singing wraps up. It's one of the sillier, most music-heavy stretches of the series.

title: Double Katana Trouble
synopsis: A fighter joins in wielding two katanas at once, awkwardly admitting the blades "aren't meant for double blades" and "look funky." Between an X-ray-vision mask and a running joke about a mask of "great distance," the heroes bicker over mask names and toe-hook tricks mid-fight. It ends on a very silly "I'm a baby" gag.

title: Rocket Breaker and a Reprise
synopsis: A hero activates his "rocket breaker" attack for the first time in a while, blasting a hole in the ground, before the episode swerves into a reprise of the Care Bears song and the "fat guy" song from earlier in the saga. Mask mix-ups over an Akaku and a mysterious mask add to the confusion. It's a musical, gag-filled callback episode.

title: One More Minute Without a Mask
synopsis: The heroes explain their own power system: knocked out as Toa, they transform into more powerful Toa Nuva, and once-per-battle Suva attacks like a waterfall or tidal wave turn the tide. Facing defeat, the team vows to keep fighting "for one more minute" even without their masks on. A stray cartoon reference and a promise that "Dr. Senor takes the floor" close things out on a lighter note.

title: Awakening the Bohrok-Kal
synopsis: Baraka-style fighters bite, pull, and vibrate their way through a battle, awakening a dormant Bohrok-Kal with a Krona and bragging about their sonic shatter powers. Between color banter ("orange is so my color") and a joke about being built from scrap parts nicknamed "Scrappy," the fighters trade elemental power boasts. It ends on an absurd runaway gag about finally being able to touch one's own toe.

title: Shiny Heads and Bohrok-Kal Trouble
synopsis: Family bickering over who's the most annoying (complete with a hard-fought "shiny heads" static contest and a wrestling match over a mask-turned-football) gives way to a real fight as Bohrok-Kal attack. The heroes trade vacuum-power and elemental blasts with Makuta's forces, taking down one Bohrok-Kal while bracing for more to come.

title: A Lesson in Magnetism
synopsis: The Bohrok-Kal battle rages on with telekinesis, vacuum blasts, and a warning about the dangers of touching anyone's mask in reality. Between hits, the heroes pause to actually explain how magnetism works, walking through positive and negative charges to figure out how to pull Makuta's claws apart.

title: Charging the Finishing Blow
synopsis: A short, electric stretch as one of the heroes powers up with elemental energy for a strike on Makuta. Sparks, sound effects, and a dramatic countdown build toward what's billed as the end for their enemy.

title: Legends of the Kanohi Masks
synopsis: Mid-battle, the fighters trade beam attacks and trash-talk over a lost Krana before getting sidetracked into legend and lore -- the mythical masks of shadow and light, and what happens to your personality when you swap masks. It devolves into a goofy singalong before somebody's mask starts looking suspiciously like pudding.

title: Soda Cannons and Stolen Krana
synopsis: Soda-cannon jokes and hairspray gags open a scrappy, silly battle full of hair-pulling, name-calling, and ninja-move bragging. The heroes corner a captured creature, debate healing up before the next fight, and swap a story about baby Ella and her "pretzel" mask trophies.

title: Parental Discretion Advised
synopsis: A full, deadpan movie-theater-style warning opens the episode -- violence ahead, young kids should leave the room, no blood promised but discretion advised anyway. Once the announcements wrap, the real showdown begins as Makuta confronts his enemies after sneaking in and causing damage, setting up a battle five challenges in the making.

title: The Toa of Light Rises
synopsis: Makuta and his enemies trade philosophy as much as blows -- destiny, vengeance, and what a Matoran can become. Amid talk of a legendary Mask of Light and Mask of Destiny, a hero transforms into the Toa of Light, and the family declares this the battle that decides who's truly dominant.

title: Powering the Supernova Beam
synopsis: Makuta unveils a monstrous new form and unleashes his Rahkshi, still at full strength, while the heroes size up his defenses. Between slashes and taunts, one fighter begins charging a Hyper Supernova Beam meant to finish Makuta once and for all.

title: Behold the Void of Makuta
synopsis: The Toa of Light recalls the old days of the Power Team and the Portal of Chaos as he closes in on Makuta, quoting a line about masks unmasking who you really are. Makuta obliges -- dissolving into smoke to reveal his true form, "the void," and daring the heroes to fight through his Rahkshi first.

title: The Black Hole Beam
synopsis: In a short, breathless final push, the Toa of Light calls on the combined power of every hero in the Super Family, fusing it with the Hyper Supernova Beam. The result: a "Super Chaotic Black Hole Beam of Destruction" that brings the long fight with Makuta to its end.

title: Rise, Makuta
synopsis: A blink-and-you'd-miss-it beat with almost no narration -- just a single ominous line hinting Makuta isn't finished yet. Whatever happens here plays out in silent stop-motion action rather than words.

title: Donuts, Announcements, and Story Time
synopsis: A new tape opens with its own mock movie-theater announcements and a surprise gymnastics demo before settling into cozy behind-the-scenes territory, including a rundown of who's getting repaired at "the shop" after a rough crash. The real centerpiece is a chaotic homemade-snack cooking segment -- glazed donuts, chunky sauces, and a running joke about an ancient jar of topping -- capped with a wink that a new evil is coming, but not for twenty years.

title: Roll Call for Lego Island
synopsis: Story time turns into big news: instead of the planned trip to Mata Nui, the family's actually headed to Lego Island for a beach vacation. Morning ritual follows -- a full roll call of the baby characters, the Pledge of Allegiance, and the start of a silly homeschool lesson in spelling and math.

title: The Secret Hunt for a Puppy
synopsis: Lessons wrap up, bedtime hits, and then a mysterious noise outside sends two of the kids sneaking out after dark to investigate. They creep through a secret passageway and a "forest," worried about scaring off whatever they're chasing, until they finally track down a scruffy, hungry stray puppy.

title: Shelby Comes Home
synopsis: The rescued puppy gets a name -- Shelby -- along with a towel, a too-long sweater, and a lot of affectionate teasing about his size and appetite. With the newest member of the family settled in, attention turns to packing the limousine and getting ready for the big beach trip.

title: Beach Hermits and Buried Plans
synopsis: The road trip kicks off -- crossing the big bridge, picking Stacy up from gymnastics, and rolling into the beach with Shelby along for the ride. Meanwhile the villains disguise themselves as "beach hermits" to hunt down the family and get their hands on the mysterious new Vahki before anyone else does.

title: Tubing, Cliffs, and a Corn Mystery
synopsis: Vacation life settles into a rhythm -- tubing on the water, pricey boat rides, a scenic cliff, and Shelby chasing after toys -- as the trip nears its end. A stray whiff of corn sends everyone off to investigate who's munching nearby, while the villains keep circling, still hunting for the family.

title: Vahki on the News
synopsis: A cell-phone news alert warns of mysterious two-or-four-legged Vahki creatures on the loose, sending both the heroes and the disguised villains searching the dunes and storm clouds for clues -- footprints, a bent electric fence, an abandoned soda bottle. The search breaks for a round of mini-golf and a very long-running joke about ordering French fries.

title: Blueprint for an Evil Mansion
synopsis: A roll call for the baby characters turns worried when two of them turn up "crashed," while a jumbo-crab beach day and Halloween marshmallows carry on around it. The real highlight: the villains finally find their secret hideout village and lay out, in absurd step-by-step detail, the booby-trapped mansion they're dreaming up -- TNT, whirlwinds of death, and all.

title: Fireworks and the Mind-Controlled Pet
synopsis: The villain duo keeps sketching their trap-filled dream mansion before finally cracking open a glowing shrine that unlocks the Vahki, and along the way, one of them mind-controls a creature into a new pet. The vacation winds toward its close with a windy beach walk and a storm rolling in, right around Independence Day fireworks for the Super Family.

title: The Vahki Awaken
synopsis: Between a lighthearted minnow-watching moment with Shelby and more scheming over their evil mansion blueprint, the villains finally activate the shrine and awaken a Vahki -- programmed as police, not evil, much to their annoyance. A scrappy, joke-filled skirmish breaks out as the Vahki refuses to be recruited to their side.

title: One More Vahki to Find
synopsis: The freshly awakened Vahki clashes with the villains in a silly, disc-throwing, karate-chopping fight before making its escape. The vacation winds down as the family starts packing up, and the transcript trails off into a long stretch of unrelated background broadcast audio picked up by the camera.

title: Tuned to the Wrong Channel
synopsis: This stretch of tape is almost entirely a golf tournament broadcast -- commentary from a U.S. Amateur final -- picked up in the background rather than any narrated Super Family action. No battles, no toys, just the camcorder quietly catching whatever was playing on TV nearby.

title: Still Tuned Out
synopsis: The golf broadcast continues uninterrupted, tracking the tournament's final holes with no Super Family narration in sight. The tape cuts out on an unrelated, unclear snippet of dialogue about being "over budget" -- background noise rather than any scripted toy-battle scene.
